1.note: Jeremiah is using the phrase translated as **Now it happened** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

The **seventh** month of the Hebrew calendar includes the last part of September and the first part of October on Western calendars. You could convert the Hebrew day and month into an approximate date on the calendar that your culture uses. However, the Jews used a lunar calendar, so if you use a solar calendar, the date will be different every year, and the translation will not be entirely accurate. So you may just want to give the number of the day and the name of the month on the Hebrew calendar and say in a footnote approximately what time of year that is on your calendar.

1.q: יִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן נְתַנְיָ֣ה בֶן אֱלִישָׁמָ֣ע & גְּדַלְיָ֥הוּ בֶן אֲחִיקָ֖ם
1.note: The words **Ishmael**, **Nethaniah**, **Elishama**, **Gedaliah**, and **Ahikam** are the names of men.

Here Jeremiah is speaking as if the descendants of the kings of Judah were **seed** that grew from a plant. It means that Ishmael was a member of the royal family. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from among the descendants of the kings]

Eating a meal together was a symbolic action by which Ishmael and his men showed that they were at peace with Gedaliah and loyal to him. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [And they ate bread there together in Mizpah as a sign that they were at peace with Gedaliah and loyal to him]

Jeremiah is using **bread** to represent food in general. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And they ate food]

2.note: The pronoun **he** refers to Ishmael, and the pronoun **him** refers to Gedaliah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and Ishmael put Gedaliah to death]

The implication is that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah to govern the land of Judah. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [whom the king of Babylon had appointed as governor over the land of Judah]

3.q: וְ⁠אֵ֣ת כָּל הַ⁠יְּהוּדִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר הָי֨וּ אִתּ֤⁠וֹ אֶת גְּדַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ בַּ⁠מִּצְפָּ֔ה וְ⁠אֶת הַ⁠כַּשְׂדִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִמְצְאוּ שָׁ֑ם אֵ֚ת אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַ⁠מִּלְחָמָ֔ה הִכָּ֖ה יִשְׁמָעֵֽאל
3.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information that **Ishmael struck** these people before the information about who these people were. Alternate translation: [And Ishmael struck all of the Judeans who were with him, with Gedaliah, in Mizpah, and the Chaldeans who were found there, the men of war]

The expression **who were found** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [whom Ishmael found there]
See how you translated the similar expression in 39:4.

The implication is that Ishmael killed these people when he **struck** them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Ishmael struck and killed]

4.note: See how you translated the similar expression “a man will not know” in 40:15. Alternate translation: [when know one knew what had happened] or [before anyone had found out what had happened]

5.note: Shaving their beards, tearing their clothes, and cutting themselves were symbolic actions by which these men showed that they were grieving deeply, probably because Jerusalem and the temple had been destroyed. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of these actions in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [ones having shaved their beards and torn their clothes and having cut themselves to show that they were grieving deeply]

Here, **hand** represents “possession.” It means that these men were carrying these offerings with them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [with them]
See how you translated the similar expression in 17:26.

6.note: Jeremiah is repeating forms of the verb **go** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. Here this indicates that Ishmael kept on weeping as he walked along. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [weeping all the way as he went]

The implication is that Ishmael was deceiving these men, since he had already killed Gedaliah. He wanted them to follow him into the city so that he could kill them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [that he deceitfully said to them]

7.note: Jeremiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [that Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, slaughtered them and threw them into the midst of the cistern]

8.note: The expression **were found** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [But there were ten men among them]

The implication is that these men were offering to give Ishmael the food supplies that they had hidden in the field if he would let them live. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [for we will give you the stores that we have in the field]

Here Jeremiah is speaking as if the other men who came with these ten men were their **brothers**. It means that they were their fellow countrymen. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in the midst of their fellow countrymen]

9.q: וְ⁠הַ⁠בּ֗וֹר אֲשֶׁר֩ הִשְׁלִ֨יךְ שָׁ֤ם יִשְׁמָעֵאל֙ אֵ֣ת כָּל פִּגְרֵ֣י הָ⁠אֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִכָּה֙ בְּ⁠יַד גְּדַלְיָ֔הוּ ה֗וּא אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשָׂה֙ הַ⁠מֶּ֣לֶךְ אָסָ֔א מִ⁠פְּנֵ֖י בַּעְשָׁ֣א מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל
9.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **King Asa** making the cistern before the information about Ishmael throwing the corpses into it. Alternate translation: [And King Asa had made a cistern from the face of Baasha, the king of Israel, and it was into that cistern that Ishmael had thrown all of the corpses of the men whom he had struck down in the hand of Gedaliah]

Jeremiah is using **in the hand of ** as a common expression of the culture. Here this expression could mean: (1) that Ishmael killed these men because of Gedaliah, that is, because they were loyal to him. Alternate translation: [because they had supported Gedaliah] (2) that Ishmael killed these men beside Gedaliah, that is, along with him. If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [along with Gedaliah]

Jeremiah is using **from the face of Baasha** as a common expression of the culture to mean “because of the threat from Baasha.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [because of the threat from Baasha]

Jeremiah is using the adjective **slain** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [filled it with the men whom he had killed]

10.note: The expression **having been left** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the ones whom the Babylonians had left in Mizpah]

Here Jeremiah is speaking as if the Ammonite people were the **sons** of their ancestor **Ammon**. It means that they were his descendants. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the descendants of Ammon]

11.note: The words **Johanan** and **Kareah** are the names of men.

11.q: אֵ֤ת כָּל הָֽ⁠רָעָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה יִשְׁמָעֵ֖אל בֶּן נְתַנְיָֽה
11.note: If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **evil**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [how wickedly Ishmael, the son of Nethaniah, had acted]

12.note: The implication is that these were the soldiers whom Johanan and the captains commanded. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [all of the soldiers whom they commanded]

13.note: The implication is that **all of the people who were with Ishmael** were the people whom he had taken captive at Mizpah, not his own men. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [all of the people whom Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah]
See how you translated the names **Johanan** and **Kareah** in 41:11.

15.note: The implication is that these **eight men** were some of Ishmael’s own men who had been with him. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [with eight of his own men]
Here, **face** represents “presence.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from Johanan’s presence]
See how you translated this same phrase in 41:10.

16.note: The pronoun **he** refers to Johanan. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [whom Johanan had brought back from Ishmael]
See how you translated “struck” 41:3. Alternate translation: [he had killed] or [he had murdered]

16.q: גְּבָרִ֞ים אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַ⁠מִּלְחָמָ֗ה וְ⁠נָשִׁ֤ים וְ⁠טַף֙ וְ⁠סָ֣רִסִ֔ים
16.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **the mighty men of war, and women and little ones and eunuchs** with the information about **all of the remnant of the people**, since this list describes who those people were. Alternate translation: [including the mighty men of war, and women and little ones and eunuchs]

17.note: The words **Geruth Kimham** are the name of a place.

18.note: Jeremiah is using **from their face** as a common expression of the culture to mean “from the presence of” in the first occurrence and “because of” in the second occurrence. If this phrase does not have these meanings for your readers, you could use a comparable expression or expressions from your language that do have these meanings, or you could state the meanings plainly. Alternate translation: [to get away from the Chaldeans, because they were afraid of what the Chaldeans would do to them]

18.q: כִּ֥י יָרְא֖וּ מִ⁠פְּנֵי⁠הֶ֑ם כִּֽי הִכָּ֞ה יִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן נְתַנְיָ֗ה אֶת גְּדַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן אֲחִיקָ֔ם
18.note: The word **for** introduces the reason why the people wanted to get away from the Chaldeans, and the word **because** introduces the reason why they were afraid of them. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use connecting words in your language that make these reasons clearer.
See how you translated “struck” in Jeremiah 41:16. Alternate translation: [had murdered]
